intro: Zafferana Etnea's great tree is the Ilice di Carrinu, a holm oak at about 950 metres on Etna's eastern slope that a lava flow approached in the winter of 1950 and stopped about 100 metres short of. The Sicilian register measures its trunk at 4.9 metres round and its height at 18 metres, and local writers call it the biggest holm oak on Etna. Its age, roughly 700 years, is an estimate without a method. It is reached only on foot.
meta_description: The Ilice di Carrinu above Zafferana Etnea: a holm oak put at about 700 years that a 1950 lava flow stopped short of, reached on foot.
question_meta: Zafferana Etnea's oldest tree is the Ilice di Carrinu, a holm oak estimated at roughly 700 years, on Etna's eastern slope.
question_answer: The oldest tree near Zafferana Etnea is the Ilice di Carrinu, a holm oak at about 950 metres on Etna's eastern slope. Its age is usually given as roughly 700 years, an estimate without a published method, so anywhere between 500 and 800 is the honest reading.
question_context: The oak has two names, the Ilice di Carrinu after Carlino, a former owner of the land, and the Ilice du Pantanu after a marsh nearby that has since vanished. Between December 1950 and January 1951 Sicilian newspapers followed an arm of lava heading for it, which stopped about 100 metres short. The Sicilian register measures the trunk at 4.9 metres round and the tree at 18 metres tall. Etnanatura describes it as the last of a holm oak forest that once linked the mountain's eastern and northern slopes, and in 1982 the State Forestry Corps, listing 22,000 Italian trees of interest, put it among 150 of exceptional value. The usual age of about 700 years has no method behind it. The tree stands in Etna Park and is reached on foot by a signed path that starts 350 metres along via Spoto at Caselle, above Zafferana, about 3 to 4 kilometres out and back. One wooden gate has to be climbed over, and the last stretch past a ruined shelter is fainter. Via Scuto and the Milo side are other ways in.

trees.story:
In the winter of 1950, an arm of Etna's lava kept heading for this holm oak, and stopped about 100 metres short. Sicilian newspapers tracked its approach in reports from December 1950 into January 1951. The oak is still standing, at about 950 metres on the volcano's eastern slope.

It goes by two names: the Ilice di Carrinu, after Carlino, a former owner of the land, and the Ilice du Pantanu, after a marsh nearby that has since vanished. The Sicilian register measures the trunk at 4.9 metres round and the tree at 18 metres tall, and local writers call it the biggest holm oak on Etna. Etnanatura describes it as the last of a holm-oak forest that once linked the mountain's eastern and northern slopes. In 1982 the State Forestry Corps listed 22,000 Italian trees of interest and put this one among 150 of exceptional value.

Its age, roughly 700 years, is an estimate given without a method, so anywhere between 500 and 800 is the honest reading.

You reach it on foot. The signed path starts 350 metres along via Spoto at Caselle, above Zafferana; via Scuto and the Milo side are the other ways in. Count on 3 to 4 km out and back through woodland, about 1 hour 40. One wooden gate has to be climbed over, and the last stretch, past a ruined shelter, is fainter. The Castagno dei Cento Cavalli at Sant'Alfio stands about 8 km to the north, by a different road.

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF) / Regione Siciliana elenco, sheet 01/M139/CT/19, D.M. n. 5450 of 19/12/2017

trees.access: Free. On foot only: a signed footpath through woodland in Etna Park zone B, roughly 3 to 4 km out and back, about 1h40 (etnanatura: from via Spoto at Caselle, Zafferana, 350 m along via Spoto the trail starts at a sign; etnaest.com says it can be reached by car to Via Scuto, trail under 2 km). etnanatura notes one wooden gate to climb over on that route and a fainter final stretch past a ruined shelter; Zafferana Pro Loco lists the tree and its paths on its own pages, and guided groups walk to it (PFM Association walk 24 May 2025). Ground ownership not stated by any source; path is signed and used by guides.
trees.transport: No practical public transport to the trailhead. By car from Zafferana Etnea (about 5 km) to via Spoto / via Scuto at Caselle; Milo is the other trailhead. About 22 km by road from Taormina, roughly 45 minutes by car; labelled day trip from Taormina or Catania.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk, 4.9 metres round, under a crown about 30 metres across. It stands where the signed footpath from Caselle ends, just past a ruined shelter.
